judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The visually hidden label 'E-mail' of the footer newsletter form has for="form-field-email". That id appears twice, on the lead form's e-mail field and on the footer field, so the label names the first one, as the claim says (that field's name becomes 'E-mail E-mail'). For 4.1.2, though, no component ends up without an accurate name and role. The footer field is still a textbox with the name 'Digite seu e-mail', from its placeholder (the snapshot's browser name), and the lead form's field keeps an accurate, if doubled, name. A label is not a user interface component itself. Duplicate ids as such were a 4.1.1 matter, which the 2023 errata treats as always satisfied for HTML. They fail 4.1.2 only when they leave a component with a missing or wrong name, which is not the case here. Because the label is screen-only, no visible relationship is lost either. The rule flags the broken reference as a failure in itself, which is stricter than the criterion. My own fetch of the live page (curl with a browser user agent, itself automated) returns the same markup for this element as the snapshot, so nothing found differs for this claim; the screenshot is taller than the snapshot's layout (the course grid grew after the tree was read), which does not touch it.
